plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large golden-yellow flower heads that track the sun when young. Widely cultivated for seeds, oil, and ornamental use, and also growing wild in prairies and roadsides across North America.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: North America, Europe, and temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not a single flower but a composite of hundreds to thousands of tiny florets arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies. Fields of lavender are at peak bloom or being harvested in late July and early August.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August)
plants.location: Mediterranean region, Provence in France, England, and temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and its name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large, round leaves held above the water and spectacular pink or white flowers up to 30 cm wide. The blooms open in the morning and close at night, rising from muddy ponds and lakes.
plants.location: Asia, including India, China, Japan, and Vietnam, and northern Australia
plants.funFact: Lotus flowers can regulate their own temperature, staying around 30-35°C even when the air is much cooler, and lotus seeds have been germinated after more than 1,000 years of dormancy.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with giant flower heads surrounded by colorful bracts, resembling a crown. Native to the fynbos of South Africa, where it blooms during the Southern Hemisphere's late winter and early spring, with flowering beginning around this time.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (roughly May to November, with peak from August)
plants.location: Fynbos region of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The King Protea is the national flower of South Africa, and the protea family is so ancient that it dates back to before the supercontinent Gondwana split apart.
